result.title: Adaptive Expert Guidance for Efficient On-Policy Reinforcement Learning
result.summary: With massively parallel simulation, on-policy Reinforcement Learning methods such as PPO have become standard in many domains. However, learning from scratch is sample-inefficient and fails to exploit the potential existence of a suboptimal expert, such as a heuristic, a model-based controller, or a policy trained on a related task. Such an expert is often available and can guide early training, but its sub-optimality limits final performance. The challenge then becomes balancing expert guidance against learning from rewards. Existing methods set the expert's influence through a blending weight, a schedule, or an evaluation-driven curriculum. Alternatively, they adapt it with additional learned components such as critics over expert actions or auxiliary agents. However, none optimizes it using the same on-policy objective as the policy itself. We propose a method in which the learner and the expert alternate control within each training episode, and the expert's share of control is a single learnable parameter optimized jointly with the policy. The learner benefits from the expert early in training, but its share of control declines as the learner becomes more competent, until eventually vanishing completely. This leaves the learner acting alone and better than the suboptimal expert. We evaluate our method on 34 tasks across two benchmarks, spanning discrete and continuous action spaces, using both learned and model-based experts. Our method improves sample efficiency over guided and unguided baselines while requiring minimal hyperparameter variation. The expert's share decays to zero as the learner improves, vanishing when the expert is no longer useful.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究并行仿真下的 on-policy RL 样本效率问题：让学习器与次优专家在每个训练回合内交替控制，并把专家控制占比设为一个可学习参数，与策略用同一 on-policy 目标联合优化，使专家影响随学习器变强而衰减至零。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「可学习控制占比随能力提升衰减至消失」的机制，可能与 LVR 中 latent 计算何时启用、THINK/LOOK 预算分配与停止决策的轻量可学习门控有概念联系，可供核查。
